input.name: Red Bull Lyric Lab
input.tagline: Everything must go — especially the feelings. Write it, record it, take it home.
input.audience: Qloo reads Phoebe Bridgers' fans as 25–29 and female, described as Heartbreak, Expressive, Personal Reflection, Singer & Songwriter, Introspective and Guitar. Their top brands are Fender, Dr. Martens, Gibson, Urban Outfitters, Vans and Polaroid. Their venue taste is Casual, Inviting, Community Focused and Charming, and their customer identities are Health-Conscious and Art Enthusiasts.
input.gap: Red Bull's default is a loud, sports-and-DJ activation for its own 35–44, male followers (GoPro, Monster Energy, Supercross LIVE!). The overlap fit is only 36, with no shared top-15 brands or artists and an age similarity of 0.45. Lyric Lab gives Red Bull a quiet, creative, songwriter-friendly role instead: it provides the space to write and record, not the volume. The Dollarama stays a dollar-store joke, but it is now a lived-in room for sad songs.
input.offer: Free entry with RSVP. Red Bull Zero and Sugar-Free served as light spritzers, with a non-alcoholic option for the Health-Conscious crowd. The line-up moment is the Lyric Lab booth: a 60-second guided songwriting prompt, then a recording on a Fender amp. Each fan takes home a flexi-disc or QR download of their take, a risograph lyric zine and a Fender pick pack in a Red Bull blue tin, all free. Optional $5 merch at the bar.

design_choices.choice: One large illuminated "Red Bull" sign on the back wall above a cobalt blue bar and a matching blue recording booth. Blue is the only brand colour; everything else follows the fans.
Warm wood planks, layered rugs, mismatched velvet sofas and floor cushions. These replace the white vinyl tiles and read as a living room, not a sports bar.
The left slatwall becomes a collage of gig posters, Polaroids and hung guitars, with Fender and Gibson as the reference brands. Polaroid is one of the fans' top brands in audience_overlap.
Warm bulb strings and paper lanterns replace the fluorescent tubes, for a lively and welcoming room.

check_audience_fit flagged Cozy, Industrial, Artistic, Old School, Retro and Chic as mismatches, because they skew 55+ female against the 25–29 female fans. I dropped them. Parisian Bistro and Vintage were only neutral, so I did not build on them. The design rests on tags that fit (Eclectic, Casual, Hipster, Beachy, Fun, Lively, Community Focused, Inviting).
A playlist weighted to the artists the fans lean toward in the shared set, with a few Red Bull-leaning picks to bridge the two crowds.
Fender pick pack and a Skullcandy listening station. Both brands are shared by the two audiences.

concept.gap: Red Bull's default is a loud, sports-and-DJ activation for its own 35–44, male followers (GoPro, Monster Energy, Supercross LIVE!). The overlap fit is only 36, with no shared top-15 brands or artists and an age similarity of 0.45. Lyric Lab gives Red Bull a quiet, creative, songwriter-friendly role instead: it provides the space to write and record, not the volume. The Dollarama stays a dollar-store joke, but it is now a lived-in room for sad songs.
concept.offer: Free entry with RSVP. Red Bull Zero and Sugar-Free served as light spritzers, with a non-alcoholic option for the Health-Conscious crowd. The line-up moment is the Lyric Lab booth: a 60-second guided songwriting prompt, then a recording on a Fender amp. Each fan takes home a flexi-disc or QR download of their take, a risograph lyric zine and a Fender pick pack in a Red Bull blue tin, all free. Optional $5 merch at the bar.

design_choices.choice: One large illuminated "Red Bull" sign on the back wall above a cobalt blue bar and a matching blue recording booth. Blue is the only brand colour; everything else follows the fans.
Warm wood planks, layered rugs, mismatched velvet sofas and floor cushions. These replace the white vinyl tiles and read as a living room, not a sports bar.
The left slatwall becomes a collage of gig posters, Polaroids and hung guitars, with Fender and Gibson as the reference brands. Polaroid is one of the fans' top brands in audience_overlap.
Warm bulb strings and paper lanterns replace the fluorescent tubes, for a lively and welcoming room.

check_audience_fit flagged Cozy, Industrial, Artistic, Old School, Retro and Chic as mismatches, because they skew 55+ female against the 25–29 female fans. I dropped them. Parisian Bistro and Vintage were only neutral, so I did not build on them. The design rests on tags that fit (Eclectic, Casual, Hipster, Beachy, Fun, Lively, Community Focused, Inviting).
A playlist weighted to the artists the fans lean toward in the shared set, with a few Red Bull-leaning picks to bridge the two crowds.
Fender pick pack and a Skullcandy listening station. Both brands are shared by the two audiences.
